title: talos(save-secrets.sh): a failed sops encryption truncates secrets.enc to zero bytes and the script still exits 0

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
## Problem

`infra/talos/01b.us/save-secrets.sh` — the script that persists the Talos cluster's secrets to their only encrypted copy, `secrets.enc` — writes that copy non-atomically **and** masks the failure:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
tar czf - ./secrets | base64 >secrets.tmp
sops --encrypt secrets.tmp >secrets.enc
rm secrets.tmp
```

- `save-secrets.sh:3`: the shell truncates `secrets.enc` **before** `sops` runs, so any encryption failure (missing/expired sops key, sops error, disk full, interruption) leaves the encrypted copy empty or partial.
- The script has **no `set -e` / `pipefail`** at all (the house style in this repo's sibling scripts, e.g. `infra/dns/*.sh` and `init-talos.sh` itself, is `set -Eexuo pipefail`). After `sops` fails, `rm secrets.tmp` (line 4) still runs and succeeds, so the script **exits 0** — the failure is silent.
- The caller trusts that exit code: `init-talos.sh` (which runs under `set -Eexuo pipefail`) invokes `./save-secrets.sh` at lines 14 and 148 and proceeds with cluster bootstrap on the assumption the secrets were saved.

## Evidence

`infra/talos/01b.us/save-secrets.sh` @ `9c06d0c8a4` (full file, 4 lines, quoted above):

- `secrets.enc` is 43,916 bytes and is the **only** persistent copy: `.gitignore` ignores `secret*` and excepts exactly `!secrets.enc`; the plaintext `./secrets` directory is gitignored, and `load-secrets.sh` can only regenerate it **from** `secrets.enc`.
- Verified this run on the laptop (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-talos-save`, real `save-secrets.sh` copied verbatim — md5 identical to the repo file — stub `sops` on PATH):
  - Stub `sops --encrypt` exits 1: `save-secrets.sh` exits **0** and `secrets.enc` goes from 30 bytes to **0 bytes**.
  - Control (stub `sops --encrypt` succeeds): exit 0, `secrets.enc` holds the new ciphertext, `secrets.tmp` removed.
  - Load path probed for contrast: a failing `sops --decrypt` in `load-secrets.sh` exits 2 via `tar`, so the load side is **not** silently masked in that shape — the defect is specific to the save side.

## Why it matters

`secrets/` holds the cluster's identity material (`secrets.yaml` from `talosctl gen secrets`, plus the generated controlplane/worker configs and talosconfig). `secrets.enc` is the sole durable, committed copy of it. Zeroing it on a transient sops failure destroys the cluster's secrets — a re-run of `init-talos.sh` would generate a **new** cluster identity rather than recover the old one — and because the script reports success, the operator only discovers the loss the next time `load-secrets.sh` is needed, possibly after the plaintext directory has been cleaned up. The intermediate `secrets.tmp` is also an unencrypted base64 tarball of the same secrets: it is removed on the happy path, but nothing guarantees its cleanup if the script is interrupted mid-run.

Related but distinct: #6536 covers the same non-atomic pattern in `infra/dns/save.sh` (different script, different state of record, and that script at least exits non-zero on failure). This issue is the Talos counterpart, with the additional failure-masking defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `save-secrets.sh` encrypts to a temporary file in the same directory and atomically renames it over `secrets.enc` only after `sops` exits 0 and the temp file is non-empty; a failed encryption leaves the previous `secrets.enc` byte-identical.
- [ ] The script fails loudly: `set -Eeuo pipefail` (house style) or equivalent explicit checks, so a `tar` or `sops` failure exits non-zero and `init-talos.sh` stops instead of proceeding.
- [ ] Plaintext-bearing intermediates (`secrets.tmp` and any new temp ciphertext) are cleaned up on failure and on interruption (e.g. an EXIT trap), without touching the live `secrets.enc`.
- [ ] A regression probe/test with a failing `sops --encrypt` stub shows `secrets.enc` unchanged **and** a non-zero exit; a succeeding stub shows the new ciphertext in place; `load-secrets.sh` still round-trips a saved `secrets.enc`.
